fields.title: Filipino Nurses: The Greatest Migration Story Never Told
fields.description: While the notion of a Filipino nurse may be considered a stereotype in the United States, compelling global and societal factors reveal a lesser-told migration story involving thousands of immigrants who now call themselves Americans. Author Angel Abcede will examine these forces as well as bring to life the stories of his mother and aunts, all of whom were Filipino nurses. If you're a Filipino in the U.S., you more than likely are or have a family member who is a nurse or involved in healthcare. This seminar will tell you why.
facilitators: Filipino American Historical Society of Chicago

fields.title: AZA Essentials - Service Project
fields.description: Join AZA Essentials for an interactive community service workshop where you’ll learn about our mission and the impact we are making in the Chicagoland community. During this hands-on experience, volunteers will assemble hygiene kits filled with essential items such as toothbrushes, toothpaste, soap, mini towels, razors, feminine hygiene products, and deodorant. These kits will be distributed to the impoverished youth and individuals experiencing homelessness throughout the Chicagoland area. Volunteers will have the opportunity to make a meaningful difference while learning more about the importance of access to basic hygiene essentials. Volunteer hours will be provided to participants who complete the workshop!

fields.title: Exploring Filipino Immigration Climate in the U.S.
fields.description: In this presentation, we will we covering the history of Filipino immigration to the U.S., as well as the process of assimilation. We will open the space to discussion throughout various points of the presentation. Then, we will transition to current immigration climate in the U.S., with a focus on the Asian American community. We will also ask members of the audience to open up about their experiences, if they choose to. We will then switch to I-CAUSE and its mission, and finish up with resources available on campus open to all students.

fields.title: Healing, Care, and the Filipinx Experience: The Magic of Knowing
fields.description: The Filipinx American is often found at the site of care: cooking, nursing, volunteering, educating, guiding, supporting, serving. What can it look like when our community cares for each other, and how can we navigate our shared historical trauma to lead to our collective power? This workshop will use tools and activities from Asian American Studies to understand healing through a Filipinx lens, such as tarot and affirmation cards, radical listening, ancestral knowledge, and conversation circles. Together, we will create dialogue and magic to reflect introspectively and with our peers within a safe, brave space.

fields.title: Medical Missions, Rehabilitation and Relief! Going Back Home to Help Our Home!
fields.description: We'll be sharing about the importance of going to the Philippines and demonstrating how we can give back on a long term basis using medical missions by assisting in rehabilitation and providing genuine relief. You'll learn from hands on experiences of people who have assisted some of the most vulnerable communities. As well as learn how you can go back home! So you can participate in helping our kababayan and embark on an extremely meaningful and impactful experience!

fields.title: More Than Trauma: Exploring Generational Activism in the Pan-Asian Community
fields.description: Asian American narratives have long been oversaturated with stories of intergenerational trauma. Beyond the immigrant trauma narrative, moments of advocacy, community, and solidarity have lit the way for future generations. In the spirit of enchanting our bright minds, we seek to tell a different story: one that shines a spotlight on the generations of activism before and ahead of us. We call on you to engage this vibrant history and take lessons from the past to imagine brighter futures for us all.
facilitators: Asian American Coalition to Combat Oppression, Racism, and Discrimination (ACCORD) at UIUC

fields.title: Impacts of A.I. on the Filipino People and Our Environment
fields.description: Want to learn more about current news in the Philippines? PAX-SILICA is an initiative to secure critical resources needed in A.I. production. Join Kabataan Alliance and its impact on the Filipino Community both here and in the Philippines!

fields.title: Defend Migrants: Youth & Students Fight Against Fascism!
fields.description: This workshop will give an overview of Tanggol Migrante campaigns, both locally and nationally and how youth and students have been able to advocate and fight for Filipino migrants facing detention, deportation, and fascist repression. Join this workshop to learn more about the current situation of Filipino migrants, the conditions of the Philippines and why Filipinos leave home in the first place, and the ongoing neglect of the U.S. & Philippine government.

fields.title: Bridging Generations
fields.description: Part of growth of a child is the expansion of their life beyond the constraints, the influences, and eventually the reach of their parents. But for the children of immigrant Filipino Americans, this path sometimes draws children away from the Filipino culture their immigrant parents (and/or past immigrant relatives) cherished and clung on to so deeply even after settling in the United States. This workshop is a personal look at the journey of the facilitator as a 2nd generation Filipino American navigating his relationship with his parents starting with his childhood (and hating being Filipino) though the twilight and passing of his parents and learning what it means to bridge the generations between them.

fields.title: The Evolution of Filipino Folk Dance
fields.description: The Philippines has a rich history of movement and storytelling that reflects centuries of colonial rule, migration, conflict, and cross-cultural influence. In this workshop, we want to educate people on the five suites of traditional Filipino dance, where these suites came from and what distinguishes them culturally, as well as stylistically. We want to teach how the aforementioned rich history of the Philippines has driven dances within these suites to grow and evolve. Culture is not produced in a vacuum, the world around us and the conditions that we live under have tangible impacts on how we express ourselves and engage with one another, and we aim to show that through Filipino dance.

fields.title: PSA 101: Introduction to the MAFAsphere and Beyond
fields.description: A high energy, Jeopardy style trivia workshop designed to build awareness and connection across the MAFAsphere. Attendees compete in teams to answer questions spanning geography, history, culture, and fun facts about Filipino Student Associations throughout the Midwest. In addition to the friendly competition, this session gives students a broader picture of the network they're part of, introducing them to schools and communities beyond their own campus and sparking curiosity to connect further.

fields.title: Introduction to Philippine Music—from the indigenous, colonial, to post colonial heritage
fields.description: In this presentation, I cover three genres of Philippine music reflecting the indigenous colonial and post colonial heritages: rondalla with harana, cordillera music from the Kalinga ethnic group, and Maguindanao kulintang music from Mindanao, Island Philippines. Audiences get hands on with different musical instruments. Aspects of the history and the circulation of instruments related to Latin American, Western, and Southeast Asian styles of music are discussed in great detail. Woven into the presentation are footages directly from the field and from selected YouTube videos.
facilitators: Dr. Bernard Ellorin PhD of the Pakaraguian Kulintang Ensemble

fields.title: The Art of Belonging: Stories, Archives, and the Magic of Memory
fields.description: The Art of Belonging: Stories, Archives, and the Magic of Memory is an interactive workshop that explores identity, family, community, theatre, and writing through Filipino American stories. Participants will engage in dynamic conversation, reader’s theatre inspired by short stories by Bienvenido Santos, a flash fiction writing activity, and a screening of rare archival film footage documenting Filipino American life from the 1930s–1970s. Rooted in FACT’s theme, “Mahiwagahan: Enchanting our Bright Minds,” the workshop invites participants to discover the magic, power, and resilience carried in our stories of migration, memory, and belonging. This project is presented in partnership with the Filipino American Historical Society of Chicago and the Rizal Center, highlighting the importance of preserving and sharing community history. Participants will also learn how to get involved through membership, volunteer opportunities, and future community programs.

fields.title: Maximizing your Impact at Career Fairs: Stand Out, Get the Job!
fields.description: If you are searching for jobs or internships, employers consistently rate campus career fairs as one of their most effective ways to recruit talent.  Learn how to impactfully prepare, network with ease, make a lasting impression, and strategize your overall search to take advantage of the opportunities that are the right fit for you.

fields.title: Demystifying Graduate School for Filipino-Americans
fields.description: Are you hoping to navigate the confusing graduate school process with confidence? In this workshop, I will break down the application, discuss potential funding opportunities, and explore how to find programs that align with your academic and career goals. We will discuss the different types of graduate degrees, how to build your network academically, and how to create leverage. Whether you are the first in your family to pursue advanced education or just looking for community and guidance, this workshop will give you the advice and tools you need to pursue your graduate school aspirations.

fields.title: The Art of Being You
fields.description:
To be yourself is the utmost privilege. We all have our own experiences in life—our own people, environments, upbringing, quirks, and pace. To create is to express what we long to tell the world no matter how big or small, and it all starts with you. The price of art is vulnerability, and once you fully embrace who you are, you realize that YOU are all you need to create something that fills your cup. 

Before finding the places you want to work, you have to understand what makes your work yours. In this workshop, you’ll learn how to build and pitch your creative identity, embrace imperfection throughout the process, and turn the ideas in your head into something real. From there, you’ll learn how to use what makes you you to find your place in the creative world and turn your passion into a career.

fields.title: Medical Missions, Rehabilitation and Relief! Going Back Home to Help Our Home!
fields.description: We'll be sharing about the importance of going to the Philippines and demonstrating how we can give back on a long term basis using medical missions by assisting in rehabilitation and providing genuine relief. You'll learn from hands on experiences of people who have assisted some of the most vulnerable communities. As well as learn how you can go back home! So you can participate in helping our kababayan and embark on an extremely meaningful and impactful experience!

fields.title: Salamin ng Loob
fields.description: Before we can move forward, we look inward. In Salamin ng Loob, we explore the loob (inner self) that our ancestors shaped long before we knew their names — babaylan, elders, storytellers whose strength still lives in us. Through guided reflection and storytelling, you'll trace a piece of yourself back to where it came from, and practice kapwa by naming that same magic.  Come find the ancestor already within you.

fields.title: Fostering Growth and Development in Our Organisations as Ambassadors of Our Heritage: A Leadership Roundtable
fields.description: PSA UIUC President Ethan Lopez will host a private roundtable on the leadership experience featuring leaders of the delegations present at FACT. Our goal is to come out together with a greater understanding of our shared goals and struggles, renewed ideas for the growth and development of our organisations, and new connections through which we can support each other as young leaders and ambassadors of our heritage. Consul General Melanie Rita B. Diano of the Philippine Consulate General in Chicago will be present to give remarks, connect with student leaders, and gain a greater understanding of our unique perspectives as collegiate representatives.

fields.title: From Plastics to Pick-Me's: The Evolution of Girl Hate in the Media
fields.description: In this workshop, we will be discussing how classic chic flicks, such as Mean Girls and Crazy Rich Asians, have perpetuated competition amongst women by villainizing "the other woman," and romanticized passive men. We'll explore common tropes and examples within movies and pop culture and how they ingrain internalized misogyny into young girls. The goal of this workshop is to learn how to recognize these harmful tropes in media and how they can be fixed. We will then dissect ways in which we can grow to support other women by applying these concepts to real life situations.

fields.title: Breaking Into the Music Industry: How to grow your career as a music artist
fields.description: Want to pursue music and don't know where to start? This is the workshop for you! Led by self-produced & managed musical artist, Sierra Sikora, this workshop will include a personal testimonial and advice on how to pursue your dreams. Topics will include how to market yourself, find opportunities, and grow a career from nothing as an independent music artist. Focus will be primarily on the business side rather than creative process.

fields.title: Kaya Mo, Personal Finance & Retirement 101
fields.description: Kaya Mo, Personal Finance and Retirement 101 is an introductory workshop designed to help Filipino Americans build confidence around everyday money decisions and long-term financial security. Participants will learn the fundamentals of budgeting, asset classes,  debt, and an introduction to retirement accounts fundamentals like employer-sponsored plans and compound growth. The session is tailored to the realities many in our community navigate — supporting family here and abroad, first-generation wealth-building, and balancing short-term needs with long-term financial goals. No prior finance background is required; this workshop is designed for students looking for a clear, judgment-free starting point. Attendees will leave with practical next steps and resources to continue building their financial foundation.

fields.title: Urban Street Dance Workshop
fields.description: Former Chicago jazz dancer, Angel Abcede, will lead a Master Class on "old school" Hip-Hop and Urban Street Styles of dance. In his years as a Joel Hall Dancer, Mr. Abcede studied and performed numerous types of dance, including ballet, modern and urban street styles. As a Filipino American, he experienced first hand the artistry of African American choreographers from Chicago and New York, who created performance work using multiple dance disciplines. He has toured the U.S., Europe and Russia with Joel Hall and his Chicago-based jazz dance company and at this conference, will lead a participatory class reflective his lifetime in movement.
facilitators: Filipino American Historical Society of Chicago

fields.title: Creative Expression through Music Production & Songwriting
fields.description: Creative Expression through Music Production is an interactive workshop designed to help participants discover their unique creative voice through music. Attendees will learn the fundamentals of music production while exploring how sounds, melodies, rhythms, and lyrics can be used to express emotions, experiences, and personal identity. The workshop will encourage experimentation and creativity, showing that there is no single “right” way to make music or express yourself. Participants will gain hands-on insight into the creative process and learn how to turn their ideas and experiences into something they can hear and share. Ultimately, the goal is to help participants build confidence in their creativity and see music as a meaningful tool for self-expression.

fields.title: Liwan Simulator - A Crash Course
fields.description: See what it’s like to be a part of a Liwan Rehearsal :0 Participants will be able to experience singing/playing in a group setting and to see the thought behind our medley arrangement. We'll be learning a snippet from one of our past medleys, so be prepared to sing, play and have fun :D! New and experienced singers, instrumentalists, or really anyone is welcome! And feel free to bring your own equipment as well if you’re able!

fields.title: Mapping Our Migration Stories: Narrating the Experiences of the Filipino Diaspora
fields.description: A storytelling workshop where participants can share their families’ migration stories & hear about the experiences of migrant workers abroad.

fields.title: Songs from Scratch: Songwriting & Music Production 101
fields.description: Songs from Scracth will be an introductory workshop for songwriting and music production. Led by music artist Sierra Sikora, the workshop will be both informational and interactive. Participants will have a chance to try their hand at songwriting & beatmaking, and work together with others to come up with a new song from scratch.

fields.title: Creativity for the People: Advocate for a Pro-People Culture in the Philippines
fields.description: We want youth to look deeper into their own personal connection to culture and be part of a Filipino culture that advocates for a better future for all our people. Learn about the pressing issue of PAX SILICA and how it is affecting the Filipino people all over the diaspora are experiencing while unleashing your creativity to advocate for a better future.
